data.summary: Lamport regression after a union merge of one shard written by two clones with the same agent id (same hostname+dir name, or same DDFLOW_AGENT): the merged shard's tail is no longer its max ([1,2,3,4,1]), _highest_lamport reads only the tail, the next append gets lamport 2 and folds BEFORE older events — 'update X1 --title v5' leaves title v4. doctor says Healthy. Probe: two clones, DDFLOW_AGENT=sameid, merge=union pull.

Offline divergence is silently resolved by tie-break: the same item id added in two clones (task add T2 in each) or the same item claimed in two clones folds to one winner after merge; the loser's item/lease vanishes from state and doctor reports Healthy. The add-time clash check sees only the local log.

data.claim: Textually yes: per-agent shards + merge=union + content-addressed dedup merge cleanly. Semantically no: duplicate ids, double claims and a shared-name shard all merge silently wrong.
data.probe: scratchpad two-clone probes with a bare remote: same id added in both, same item claimed in both, DDFLOW_AGENT=sameid in both, then git pull --no-rebase
data.probe_output: no conflict markers; T2 kept BOB only; T1 lease Monster3-bob only; shared shard lamports [1,2,3,4,1] and newest update lost; doctor Healthy in all

data.body: Operator 2026-09-28: 'how the ddflow database can be kept persistent as part of the repo, so if I clone the repo I can continue from where we have left ... if multiple users or agents commit to the same repo, how the .ddflow information is not going to be broken and properly merged?' Research Re770238400 (two-clone probes, CONFIRMED): per-agent shards + merge=union + content-addressed dedup merge cleanly as text; semantically, duplicate ids, double claims and a shared-name shard merge silently wrong, and nothing commits the log (55 events on disk only at filing time). Bugs B28589b8b26, Bbe8ea3c684.
data.title: The in-repo event log: clone-and-continue, and safe merges across users and agents

data.body: Research Re770238400 item 1. Only two commits in history ever touched .ddflow/events; at filing time 55 events (all of B17 and B187, 21 lines of Monster3-ddflow) existed on disk only, so a fresh clone could not continue. (a) ddflow merge stages .ddflow/events/*.jsonl into the merge commit on the base branch; (b) new 'ddflow checkpoint' (CLI + MCP) commits the event shards alone, optionally pushes; (c) doctor reports N uncommitted events / untracked shards as a warning; (d) brief/next mention unpushed ddflow/<id> branches with a live lease, since in-progress code is also lost on a fresh clone. Test: a fresh clone after merge+checkpoint folds to the same state as the origin.
data.title: Commit the event log as part of the workflow: ddflow merge includes event shards, ddflow checkpoint mid-task, doctor warns on uncommitted events

data.body: Research Re770238400 item 2; bug B28589b8b26, CONFIRMED by probe: two clones with the same derived id (same hostname + dir name, e.g. ubuntu-ddflow, or same DDFLOW_AGENT) union-merge one shard to lamports [1,2,3,4,1]; _highest_lamport (infra/log.py) reads only the tail, the next append gets lamport 2, and 'update X1 --title v5' folds to v4. doctor says Healthy. Fix both ends: (a) derived identity gets a per-clone random suffix created once in .ddflow/local/ (explicit ids and DDFLOW_AGENT unchanged; existing shards keep working); (b) the clock takes the max over parsed events (read cache makes it cheap) or detects a non-monotone shard; (c) doctor flags a shard whose lamports decrease. Regression test = the probe, and it must fail on the unfixed code.
data.title: Unique agent id per clone, and a Lamport clock that does not trust the shard tail (fixes bug B28589b8b26: newest edit lost)

data.body: Research Re770238400 item 3; bug Bbe8ea3c684, CONFIRMED by probe: 'task add T2' in two clones with different content folds to Bob's only; T1 claimed in both folds to Bob's lease only; Alice's work continues unaware; doctor Healthy. The add-time clash check sees only the local log. (a) fold records a conflict when two distinct item.added events share a subject, or two live leases from different holders overlap, instead of last-writer-wins; (b) the item shows as contested in show/brief/next and doctor exits nonzero until resolved; (c) a resolve path (rename one id / release one lease), recorded as an event; (d) id allocation for multiple writers: per-writer prefix, or hash id + human alias — decide and record a decision.
data.title: Detect offline divergence instead of a silent tie-break: same id added twice, same item claimed twice -> 'contested' (fixes bug Bbe8ea3c684)

data.body: Research Re770238400 item 4. Git cannot stop two offline clones claiming one item; B191 only detects it after the fact. When online, a server-side ref create is compare-and-swap: 'git push origin <sha>:refs/ddflow/claims/<id>' is rejected if the ref exists, giving real mutual exclusion with no server. Opt-in config knob (e.g. [flow] claims = 'remote'); release/complete/expire delete the ref; heartbeat may carry the expiry in the ref's commit; refused claim exits 3 with the holder named; unreachable remote -> recorded unavailable, never silently local. Test against a local bare remote.
data.title: Opt-in cross-machine claim lock: a claim also pushes refs/ddflow/claims/<id>, atomic on the remote

data.body: Research Re770238400 item 5. Prior art git-bug keeps data under separate refs with Lamport clocks. Staying in-tree means any checkout's queue matches its code and 'ddflow replay' keeps working; the cost is noise in main's history. (a) ddflow decision add with globs .ddflow/**, .gitattributes, ddflow/infra/log.py; (b) probe whether GitHub/GitLab server-side PR merges honour .gitattributes merge=union (UNVERIFIED at filing) and document what happens if not; (c) docs: the multi-user model — what merges, what is detected (B191), what is locked (B192), that committed session prompts are visible to everyone with repo access.
data.title: Keep the event log in the main tree (not a dedicated ref): record the decision, verify forge-side merge=union, document the multi-user model

data.summary: ddflow claim <id> run from a DIFFERENT worktree of the repo adopts the caller's worktree (and its branch) as the item's tree, even when the item already records its own worktree holding unmerged commits (B17: recorded .ddflow-worktrees/B17 with 4 commits; claim from bridge-cse_01YXX... reported 'adopted — you were already in it' on branch worktree-bridge-cse_01YXX...). A merge from there would have merged nothing and lost the salvage.

data.summary: ddflow session prompt records an EMPTY prompt silently: the positional is the SESSION id and the text comes from --text or stdin, so 'ddflow session prompt "<operator words>"' (the natural reading) stores the words as a session id and reads stdin — empty at EOF -> 'recorded (0 redaction(s))' with no text; with a live stdin it blocks forever. Should refuse empty text, and refuse reading a non-tty stdin that is not a pipe/file. Hit 2026-09-28: three operator prompts recorded empty, a fourth hung >2 min.

ddflow complete prints 'NOTE: critic never ran — recorded as a coverage gap' for a critic recorded PARTIAL (B17: two Qwen passes, 3/6 and 4/6 chunks, 7 findings acted on). The note should say partial and give coverage; 'never ran' misstates what the log holds.

data.body: Operator 2026-09-28: 'Can the bugs be treated as tasks and part of the DAG tree with priority for correction by default in order to not accumulate bugs over bugs?' Today a Bug (core/model.py:239-250) is a flat record: no needs/globs/state, never in plan(); agents file fix tasks by hand (B209-B212 'fixes bugs ...'). B-bugs-first (running) already orders bug items ahead of features. This adds the missing half: (a) 'bug found' creates a fix task by default ([bugs] file_task = true): tagged bugfix, parent = the phase of the item the bug names (or a standing 'bugs' phase), globs given or inherited from that item, linked to the bug id; (b) the task's completion requires the regression test (B-bugfix-verified) and closes the bug; (c) an item whose change introduced the bug may 'need' nothing, but a feature touching the same globs waits (glob conflict) — no bugs over bugs; (d) '--no-task' for a bug fixed in the same commit it was found; (e) existing open bugs get tasks on upgrade (one-shot migration command). Test: bug found -> next offers the fix task before a same-priority feature.
data.title: Bugs are queue items: 'bug found' files a fix task in the DAG by default, and the bug closes when that task completes with a verified regression test

data.body: Operator 2026-09-28: 'after a merge of the work of few subagents the whole code should be tested for compilation, bugging, code quality and full suite test'. Today merge() lands one item at a time (api/lifecycle.py:499-624) and every item runs its own full unit_tests/bug_hunt/dedupe; the phase close is the only combined check and fires only when a whole phase is done. (a) an 'integration' gate set ([gates] integration_pipeline: build/import check, standards, unit_tests full, bug_hunt over the combined diff) run after N merges or on demand ('ddflow integrate'); (b) 'merge --batch A,B,C' lands several independent branches onto an integration ref, runs the integration pipeline once, and fast-forwards the base only if green — a red batch is bisected to the item that broke it (reuse B26's bisect idea); (c) per-item unit_tests may then be the selected subset (B16) because the batch runs the full suite; (d) the integration result is recorded against every item in the batch. Test: a batch whose second item breaks a test does not reach the base, and the culprit is named.
data.title: Batch integration: merge several finished items, then run the heavy checks ONCE on the combined tree (build/import, lint, full suite, bug hunt)

data.body: Operator 2026-09-28: 'look at the tasks/bugs as DAG, parallelize them whenever possible, do the necessary tests and merge them together and then do the full test suite'. Today plan() gives only the current ready set plus one critical_path string; the driver says only 'fan them out to parallel subagents if your harness supports it', and implement.md drives one item per iteration. (a) schedule.waves(): every open item's earliest wave given needs + glob conflicts + caps, shown in next/board (and a mermaid DAG in board); (b) implement.md and the claude-code delta gain a fan-out protocol: orchestrator claims up to slots ready items, dispatches one subagent each (Agent isolation=worktree, ddflow_identify/as_agent, explicit model), each subagent runs its item's gates with SELECTED tests and a regression test per bug, returns; orchestrator runs B-batch-integration, then the next wave; (c) reviewers stay cross-family per item. Test: waves() on a fixture DAG matches hand-computed levels, including a glob conflict that serialises two otherwise-independent items.
data.title: Plan in waves over the DAG and a subagent fan-out protocol: claim N ready items, one subagent per worktree, then batch-integrate

data.body: Operator 2026-09-28: 'Could tasks be research tasks which could generate new phases and tasks by themselves?' Today items are phase|task with one task_pipeline for all; research is a gate and a separate record (ddflow research), and agents file follow-ups by hand (today's R-records -> B189-B193 and this phase). (a) per-tag pipelines ([gates.pipelines] research = ['research', 'probe', 'proposal', 'file']) so a research-tagged task never needs implement/merge; (b) its completion carries a research record (question, probe, verdict) and a proposal: tasks and phases with titles, globs, needs, priorities; (c) 'file' gate: proposed TASKS under existing phases are added automatically, linked back (source: research id); proposed PHASES and anything outward-facing wait on a human approval gate (reuse the B82 human gate); (d) a research item may propose further research items, with a depth/budget cap so it cannot recurse unbounded; (e) recall shows the chain research -> items. Test: completing a research item with a proposal of 2 tasks + 1 phase files the tasks, parks the phase for approval.
data.title: Research items: a task kind whose outcome is a verdict plus the phases/tasks it proposes, filed into the queue (new phases behind operator approval)

data.body: Operator 2026-09-28: 'propose to the agent as a companion pre-commit with good configurations that are relevant for the project'. Research Rb5e33fdbf9: pre-commit install AFTER ddflow keeps ddflow's hook as pre-commit.legacy and still runs it; ddflow hooks install AFTER pre-commit refuses and writes nothing; docs/HANDOFF.md:70-72 already tells adopters to add check-commit/check-msg as local hooks. This repo has no .pre-commit-config.yaml; ruff/bandit/pip-audit/gitleaks/CodeQL run only in CI. (a) [[companion]] pre-commit, kind cli, gates standards (+ security where hooks cover it), consent rule unchanged; (b) a generator: detected stack -> config (Python ruff/ruff-format reusing ruff.toml, JS eslint/prettier, Dockerfile hadolint, shell shellcheck, all: check-yaml/check-toml/check-merge-conflict/detect-private-key/end-of-file-fixer, gitleaks reusing .gitleaks.toml) with pinned revs, written only as a proposed diff; (c) ddflow's check-commit (pre-commit stage) and check-msg (commit-msg stage) as repo: local hooks; (d) hooks status/doctor recognise 'governed by pre-commit, ddflow hooks present' as installed; (e) standards gate command 'pre-commit run --from-ref <base> --to-ref HEAD'. Test: generated config for a python+docker fixture contains ruff, hadolint and both ddflow local hooks; status reports installed.
data.title: pre-commit as a companion: ddflow proposes a stack-relevant .pre-commit-config.yaml with its own checks as local hooks, and treats that as hooks-installed

data.body: Operator 2026-09-28: periodic (at least once per phase) security issues check. Today: no security gate, cadence or companion anywhere; this repo's CI runs bandit, pip-audit (advisory), gitleaks and CodeQL, invisible to ddflow. (a) GateDef 'security' (applies_to phase) in phase_pipeline; (b) cadence security_scan_every_phases = 1; (c) companions (cli, consent): bandit or semgrep (SAST), gitleaks (secrets, full history on first run), pip-audit/osv-scanner (dependency CVEs), trivy (container images/Dockerfiles); (d) a security-review.md prompt: run the tools, triage each finding CONFIRMED/false-positive with a probe, fix with a regression test or file a bug item, never silence without a recorded reason; (e) unavailable scanners recorded unavailable. Test: a phase cannot close with the security gate unrecorded; a fixture with a hard-coded key is found.
data.title: Security at least once per phase: a phase-level security gate and cadence, backed by SAST, secret, dependency-CVE and image scanners as companions

data.body: Operator 2026-09-28: 'periodically allowed to make an architectural assessment and make sure architecture is kept clean ... structured according to the user requirements or default - clean code/hexagonal architecture, and avoid writing the same code for similar functions - create modules, components, libraries'. Today architecture_review is a cadence NAME only (no template); layer rules exist only as ddflow's own tests/test_layering.py; dedupe only SUGGESTS a clone detector. (a) architecture-review.md: read the architecture decision(s), check boundaries, find parallel implementations of one operation and extract them (port/adapter, shared module), file what is too big as items; (b) init/adopt seeds a decision tagged architecture: 'ports-and-adapters + clean code unless superseded', which the operator can supersede (decision supersede); (c) layer rules generated from that decision per stack: import-linter (Python), dependency-cruiser (JS), as cli companions; (d) a clone detector companion (jscpd or pylint duplicate-code) feeding dedupe/dedupe_sweep with file:line pairs; (e) ratchets recorded per phase: duplication % and layer-violation count may not rise (ties into B20 inventory ratchets). Test: a fixture where a phase adds a duplicate function raises the ratchet and blocks phase close.
data.title: Architecture assessment with teeth: review instructions, a default style decision (hexagonal/clean unless the operator says otherwise), generated layer rules, and duplication/violation ratchets

data.body: Operator 2026-09-28: 'potential upgrade of libraries, images, containers, dependencies ... without crashing the functionality to keep the project up to date and secure'. Today nothing (no cadence, gate or companion). (a) cadence dependency_upgrade (every phase, or every_days); (b) dependency-upgrade.md: on its own item/branch, per stack (uv lock --upgrade-package, npm outdated/update, cargo update, go get -u, Dockerfile FROM digests, CI action pins), one upgrade (or one coherent group) at a time -> full suite (fast after B-parallel-tests) + integration -> keep green, revert red, and file each red one as an item with the failure; security-driven bumps (from B-security-pass) first; majors proposed, not applied, unless the operator allows; (c) optional renovate/dependabot companion for projects that prefer bot PRs; (d) record what moved in the release notes. Test: a fixture where one of two upgrades breaks a test ends with only the green one applied and an item filed for the other.
data.title: Keep dependencies, lockfiles and container images current without breaking: a periodic upgrade pass that keeps only what stays green

data.body: Operator 2026-09-28: 'Make sure in the ddflow workflow by default we have at least one per phase review and update of the documentation to make sure the documentation and README are always up to date'. Today nothing does this: the phase pipeline is research, tasks, unit_tests, bug_hunt, dedupe, live_test, corrections, merge; the only doc check is B17's per-commit stale_docs, which catches removed/renamed names but never asks whether a NEW command, flag, knob, default or behaviour reached the README and docs. (a) GateDef 'docs' (applies_to phase, evidence required) inserted before 'merge' in the DEFAULT phase_pipeline; (b) its prompt / a shipped docs-review command (MCP prompt): take the phase's whole diff (phase base..HEAD), list every user-visible change (commands, MCP tools, flags, config knobs and defaults, outputs, install steps), check each against README and the doc globs, update what is missing or wrong in the same phase, re-run stale_docs over the phase range, check README counts/examples still hold (e.g. knob counts, command samples), and record evidence as the files changed or 'no doc-visible change' with the reason; (c) the driver's phase close names the step; (d) projects that set their own phase_pipeline keep it, and 'ddflow workflow' advises when it has no docs gate; (e) README documents the new gate. Tests: the default phase pipeline contains docs before merge; a phase cannot complete with docs unrecorded; a custom phase_pipeline without docs gets the advisory.
data.title: Every phase reviews and updates the documentation by default: a 'docs' gate in the default phase pipeline, before merge

data.rule: Before running the unit_tests gate, merge the base branch into the item branch whenever main changed .ddflow/config.toml's gate commands or the dev dependencies (e.g. the pytest-xdist '-n 48' change, 8fe68e6).
data.title: A gate command is read from the primary checkout but runs with the item branch's dependencies: merge main before unit_tests after the gate config changes
data.why: load_gates reads the primary .ddflow/config.toml, but the command executes in the item's worktree with that branch's pyproject.toml/uv.lock; a branch cut before pytest-xdist was added fails with 'unrecognized arguments: -n 48'.

data.summary: A change to a gate COMMAND on main breaks every in-flight item branch that predates its dependencies: load_gates reads the primary checkout's .ddflow/config.toml, but run_command_gate executes in the item worktree with the branch's own pyproject/uv.lock (after 8fe68e6 an older branch's unit_tests fails with 'unrecognized arguments: -n 48'). The gate should either run the config from the item's own tree, or say 'your branch is behind a gate-config change: merge the base' instead of a test failure.

data.body: Operator 2026-09-29 asked whether ddflow recommends companions at first connection/setup and asks the agent to install them with the user's approval. Audit: YES over MCP — the handshake instructions (templates/prompts/mcp_instructions.md, 'Not wired up here — propose it to the operator') list each non-usable default companion with gates, install command and URL, and carry the consent protocol (probe 'not checked' first; install only if the operator agrees; dry-run registration and show the entry; decline -> record the gates unavailable; never install unasked); 'ddflow adopt' prints companions_ready/absent; CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md carry the rule; /mcp__ddflow__install-companions walks it. GAPS: (a) the SessionStart brief (the hook path — an agent on CLI + hook without the MCP handshake) does not list missing companions at all, only the static rules-file line: add a short 'Companions not wired up' section to the brief (same actionable set as the handshake, no probing at session start, 'not checked' stated as such, pointing at install-companions); (b) README's Companion tools section never mentions the install-companions command / MCP prompt; (c) README says 'Adding a fifth' though six ship. Test: brief for a repo with a missing default companion names it and the install-companions command; README mentions install-companions.
data.title: Companions reach every agent: the session-start brief lists missing companions, and the README names install-companions (and stops saying 'a fifth')
